title: Voltage is the instructive variable: an unrelated yeast pump can replace tail V-ATPase

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Voltage is the instructive variable: an unrelated yeast pump can replace tail V-ATPase

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Membrane voltage is a coarse-grained, high-order parameter over ion channel and pump microstates: electrogenic proteins can be swapped as long as the bioelectric state is correct, e.g. the V-ATPase function in tadpole tail regeneration can be phenocopied by a yeast proton pump with no sequence or structural homology.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: electrogenic proteins can be swapped out as needed (e.g., V-ATPase complex in the tadpole tail can be phenocopied by a yeast proton pump with no sequence or structural homology, because it produces the correct physiological signal), and everything still works as long as the bioelectric state is correct [190].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities”. Scope: Xenopus tadpole tail regeneration; bioelectric control generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The rescue experiment and its critical controls are highly operational. Existing published data may resolve the specific example, but broad interchangeability and separation of voltage from pH need additional matched evidence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare tail-regeneration frequency and membrane voltage after V-ATPase disruption followed by expression of the unrelated yeast proton pump, using inactive-pump and voltage-mismatched controls. Rescue that tracks restored voltage rather than sequence identity supports voltage as the instructive variable.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matched voltage, construct expression, and regeneration records may not be public.

One substitution does not establish the general coarse-graining claim.

Proton pumps alter pH as well as voltage.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.92
discriminating power: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The homology half can be settled directly from public sequences and structures. The functional phenocopy is a specific Xenopus regeneration result published as experimental measurements, without a deposited animal-level regeneration file in these databases. Voltage as the coarse-grained instructive variable is supported only if the rescue is tied to the bioelectric state rather than to a side effect of proton pumping.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Align yeast plasma-membrane proton-pump sequences and structures with Xenopus V-ATPase subunits, and compare tadpole tail regeneration when the yeast pump is expressed in place of V-ATPase function. Absence of significant sequence and structural homology, together with rescue of regeneration and of the regenerative voltage, would support interchangeability of the voltage state; homology, or rescue without restoration of voltage, would count against voltage as the instructive variable.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A yeast pump could restore regeneration by changing pH independently of the voltage pattern the claim treats as the signal.

The tail-regeneration rescue counts are in the original experimental paper, not in UniProt or the PDB.
